title.source: UCC奶咖1969上市，方便為何還這麼難？｜品牌故事
title.text: UCC Milk Coffee launched in 1969. Why was convenience still so hard? | Brand Stories

description.source:
一罐能帶走的奶咖，還要完成哪些工作，你才喝得到？跟著UCC這款產品，從1968年前後的試作、1969上市，走到1970大阪萬博的交付，再看初代罐實際如何開孔。歷史與技術依原廠及受訪者回顧歸屬；Mira早例和含奶限定分清。畫面為原創匿名概念插圖。

description.text:
What work must happen before you can drink a can of milk coffee on the go? Follow this UCC product from prototypes around 1968 and its 1969 launch to deliveries at Osaka Expo 1970, then see how holes were actually made in the original can. Historical and technical accounts are attributed to the maker and interviewees. The earlier Mira example is distinguished from the milk-containing claim. Visuals are original anonymous concept illustrations.

大阪万博で大ヒット、累計販売本数150億本超！昭和44年から半世紀以上愛され続けるロングセラー『UCC ミルクコーヒー』誕生秘話とパッケージの変遷をご紹介 | UCC上島珈琲

c11r1h02: 上島達司後來回憶，銷售人員走進食品店，
推銷一九六九年上市的UCC奶咖。
c11r1h03: 我沒想到，方便還有這一面：做成了罐子，
也得有人肯讓它走進自己的店。
c11r1h05: 跟著UCC這款奶咖，追上市前後兩年的工廠與會場，
找出帶著走還需要什麼。
c11r1o01: 先得離開那只要還的瓶子。
UCC後來回顧，創辦人上島忠雄，曾在車站買了一瓶咖啡牛奶。
c11r1o03: 你付錢買到的飲料，喝的時間卻被容器卡住；
人要出發，剩下那一口只能留著。
c11r1o04: 在上島達司後來的訪談裡，玻璃瓶還有搬運上的麻煩：
重，而且摔破會帶來危險。
c11r1o06: 把奶咖封進不必交回的罐子，成了方向；
可是，咖啡此前真的沒被裝進罐裡嗎？
c11r1o07: 濱田市的記錄寫，一九六五年九月十四日，
米拉咖啡已在日本橋三越本店出售。
c11r1o08: 後來的產業訪談，把米拉描述為加糖、
無奶的咖啡；UCC這項試作，要把奶也放進去。
c11r1o09: UCC博物館把自家這一款，稱作世界首款含奶罐裝咖啡；
這是館方對自己商品的說法。
c11r1o11: 把開發起點記在一九六八年前後，由公司組成專案推進。
c11r1o12: 你若站在試作桌旁，面前不只是換一個容器，
還有要一起進去的咖啡和牛奶。
c11r1o13: 它們調在一起的那一刻，能看起來很像一杯奶咖；
放進罐裡之後，新的難題才出來。
c11r1t01: 後來一篇採訪報導寫，咖啡抽出液和奶混合、
封入罐裡後，奶的成分會分離，浮到上部。
c11r1t06: 我讀到這個動作才明白，試作團隊處理的，
是你平常不會盯著看的液體狀態。
c11r1t07: 你不會為了買一罐奶咖，先檢查裡面的小粒子；
這份工作得由做飲料的人先完成。
c11r1t09: 還有加熱。原廠回顧說，高熱殺菌會改變咖啡的風味，
產生不想留下的加熱氣味。
c11r1t11: 你在桌邊覺得太苦，還能自己加點奶；
封進罐裡，味道就得在你打開以前處理好。
c11r1t13: 報導寫，他們持續喝試作品，尋找咖啡、
奶和糖的成分比率，設法減少加熱後留下的味道。
c11r1w06: 那層處理對付的是罐壁帶來的變色，
讓咖啡不用直接和裸露的金屬打交道。
c11r1w07: 我覺得有意思的是，設計一杯能帶走的奶咖，
最後還得把包材的做法一起改。
c11r1w10: 原廠記下，四月開始販售；可是，
有人願意買一罐，帶離原本喝咖啡的地方嗎？
c11r1w11: 上島達司在金氏世界紀錄的訪談裡回憶，
剛開始，業界有人把罐裝咖啡當成邪道。
c11r1w17: 受訪者說，也有店家在喝過之後，願意把這種奶咖留下來賣；
先試到那一口，才有貨架上的位置。
c11r1w14: 受訪者說，訂貨慢慢從十箱，到三十箱；
這些罐子，是一點一點進到店裡的。
c11r1w15: 你在食品店原本找的是熟悉的東西，
讓新罐子先出現在那裡，才有機會被拿起來。
c11r1s01: 原廠回顧，銷售人員會在車站賣店大聲指名購買，
再把買到的罐子帶上列車。
c11r1s03: 你在車廂裡能看到的商品，
多了一個不同於咖啡杯的形狀；罐子也變成展示的地方。
c11r1s04: 我覺得這個動作很小，卻很貼題：
要讓人相信能帶著走，就得真的把它帶出去。
c11r1s05: 可是，這樣的推銷仍沒有立刻讓大家熟悉它；
哪裡能讓各地來的人，同時遇上這罐奶咖？
c11r1s19: 採訪報導寫，UCC在籌備萬博生意時，
對這個活動會有多大，起初還沒有概念。
c11r1s20: 公司內部一度只想像，來客大約十萬人；
主管真正出去看，這個判斷還站得住嗎？
c11r1s06: 隔年三月，大阪的日本萬國博覽會開幕，
原本要逐家店介紹的商品，有了另一個接觸場域。
c11r1s07: 後來接受採訪的UCC館長說，
他們沿著咖啡生產國的聯繫，去接觸參展的國家。
c11r1s08: 展館裡的咖啡店和餐飲空間，需要供貨；
UCC本來就在做的咖啡生意，這時派上了用場。
c11r1s09: 可是，簽到供貨機會，並不會自己把一罐冷飲送到攤位。
罐子要從哪裡接上會場？
c11r1s11: 奶咖先在這個配送據點冷卻，再由卡車送進會場；
採訪記述，為此準備了多台車。
c11r1s14: 會場裡，來客開始拿起這種罐裝飲料；
原廠留下的當時照片，也能看到人手裡的奶咖罐。
c11r1s15: 來自各地的人，把喝過的經驗帶回家鄉；
那罐飲料的消息，跟著旅程走出了會場。
c11r1s16: 採訪還說，來客拿罐的樣子，
被電視帶進家庭，讓沒到現場的人也看見了。
c11r1s17: 連原先不願理會這罐奶咖的通路，也開始來要貨。
c11r1d02: UCC主管在採訪裡說，為了貨一做出來就運走，
工廠外出現了等待出貨的卡車。
c11r1d03: 你買的是一罐，配送端卻得一批批接貨；
多出來的需要，最後落在工廠門外。
c11r1d07: 上島達司的回憶，也把鐵道弘濟會的採用列為轉點，
奶咖於是有了接觸更多旅客的通路。
c11r1d11: 原廠初代罐的說明，寫的是用專用開孔器在罐頂開孔；
c11r1d12: 一邊是飲口，另一邊是空氣孔；喝的人要用它，
還得有能把這些入口打開的工具。
c11r1ct1: 這款奶咖把喝咖啡的地點帶走，卻沒有省掉讓你喝到的工作；
那些工作，被接到製造、配送和罐頂。
c11r1ct2: 你第一次喝罐裝飲料，記得是別人替你開好，
還是你自己打開？留言告訴我。
c11r1ct3: 想看懂熟悉物品怎麼把方便交到你手上，
歡迎訂閱，一起看那些小動作背後的選擇。

lines.source: 如果是你的小店，願不願意先放三箱奶咖，讓它占住貨架？
lines.text: If it were your little shop, would you give three cases of milk coffee some shelf space?

lines.source: 上島達司後來回憶，銷售人員走進食品店，推銷一九六九年上市的UCC奶咖。
lines.text: Tatsushi Ueshima later recalled salespeople entering food shops to sell UCC Milk Coffee, launched in 1969.

lines.source: 我沒想到，方便還有這一面：做成了罐子，也得有人肯讓它走進自己的店。
lines.text: I hadn't expected this side of convenience: once you make the can, someone still has to let it into their shop.

lines.source: 罐裡的奶，怎麼待得住？
lines.text: How could the milk stay mixed inside the can?

lines.source: 冷罐又要怎麼追上萬博的人潮？
lines.text: And how could cold cans keep up with the crowds at the Expo?

lines.source: 跟著UCC這款奶咖，追上市前後兩年的工廠與會場，找出帶著走還需要什麼。
lines.text: Follow this UCC milk coffee through factories and the Expo in the two years around its launch, to find what else portability required.

lines.source: 一杯咖啡離開店面，要怎麼讓你在別處，完整地喝到？
lines.text: Once a coffee leaves the shop, what lets you enjoy the whole drink somewhere else?

lines.source: 先得離開那只要還的瓶子。UCC後來回顧，創辦人上島忠雄，曾在車站買了一瓶咖啡牛奶。
lines.text: First, it had to leave the returnable bottle behind. UCC later recounted that its founder, Tadao Ueshima, once bought bottled coffee with milk at a station.

lines.source: 發車鈴響，他還沒喝完，就得把瓶子交回攤位，再趕上列車。
lines.text: The departure bell rang. Before he had finished, he had to return the bottle to the stall and hurry onto the train.

lines.source: 你付錢買到的飲料，喝的時間卻被容器卡住；人要出發，剩下那一口只能留著。
lines.text: You paid for the drink, but its container limited your time to drink it. When it was time to leave, that last sip had to stay behind.

lines.source: 在上島達司後來的訪談裡，玻璃瓶還有搬運上的麻煩：重，而且摔破會帶來危險。
lines.text: In a later interview, Tatsushi Ueshima described another transport problem with glass bottles: they were heavy, and breakage could be dangerous.

lines.source: 把奶咖封進不必交回的罐子，成了方向；可是，咖啡此前真的沒被裝進罐裡嗎？
lines.text: Sealing milk coffee in a can you needn't return became the direction. But had coffee really never been canned before?

lines.source: 濱田市的記錄寫，一九六五年九月十四日，米拉咖啡已在日本橋三越本店出售。
lines.text: Hamada City's records say Mira Coffee was already on sale at the Nihombashi Mitsukoshi main store on September 14, 1965.

lines.source: 後來的產業訪談，把米拉描述為加糖、無奶的咖啡；UCC這項試作，要把奶也放進去。
lines.text: A later industry interview described Mira as sweetened coffee without milk. This UCC prototype would put milk in as well.

lines.source: UCC博物館把自家這一款，稱作世界首款含奶罐裝咖啡；這是館方對自己商品的說法。
lines.text: UCC's museum calls its own product the world's first canned coffee containing milk. That is the museum's description of its own product.

lines.source: 我更想知道，咖啡和奶封在罐裡，還能維持調好的狀態嗎？
lines.text: What I want to know is whether coffee and milk could stay properly mixed once sealed inside a can.

lines.source: UCC的館長接受採訪時，把開發起點記在一九六八年前後，由公司組成專案推進。
lines.text: In an interview, UCC's museum director placed the start of development around 1968, with a company project formed to pursue it.

lines.source: 你若站在試作桌旁，面前不只是換一個容器，還有要一起進去的咖啡和牛奶。
lines.text: If you stood beside the prototype table, you would face more than a change of container: coffee and milk had to go inside together.

lines.source: 它們調在一起的那一刻，能看起來很像一杯奶咖；放進罐裡之後，新的難題才出來。
lines.text: At the moment you mix them, they can look much like a cup of milk coffee. The new difficulty appears after they go into the can.

lines.source: 放進罐裡的奶，怎麼才能留在調好的狀態？
lines.text: How could the milk in the can stay in that mixed state?

lines.source: 後來一篇採訪報導寫，咖啡抽出液和奶混合、封入罐裡後，奶的成分會分離，浮到上部。
lines.text: A later interview report says that after coffee extract and milk were mixed and canned, milk components would separate and rise to the top.

lines.source: 所以，拌在一起這個動作，要怎麼變成放得住的結果？
lines.text: So how could the act of mixing produce something that stayed mixed?

lines.source: 採訪記下的方法，是把奶的粒子做得均一，用均質化來抑制分離。
lines.text: The interview described making the milk particles uniform, using homogenization to suppress separation.

lines.source: 我讀到這個動作才明白，試作團隊處理的，是你平常不會盯著看的液體狀態。
lines.text: Only when I read about this step did I realize the team was working on a liquid state you don't normally watch closely.

lines.source: 你不會為了買一罐奶咖，先檢查裡面的小粒子；這份工作得由做飲料的人先完成。
lines.text: You wouldn't inspect tiny particles before buying a can of milk coffee. The people making the drink have to do that work first.

lines.source: 可是，讓奶不再上浮，就已經能把這杯飲料交出去嗎？
lines.text: But once the milk stops rising, is the drink ready to hand over?

lines.source: 還有加熱。原廠回顧說，高熱殺菌會改變咖啡的風味，產生不想留下的加熱氣味。
lines.text: There was also heating. The maker later explained that high-temperature sterilization changes coffee's flavor and creates unwanted heated odors.

lines.source: 奶咖要經過殺菌，喝的人卻仍會用舌頭判斷，它是不是想喝的那個味道。
lines.text: Milk coffee must be sterilized, yet the person drinking it still judges with their tongue whether it tastes right.

lines.source: 你在桌邊覺得太苦，還能自己加點奶；封進罐裡，味道就得在你打開以前處理好。
lines.text: At a table, you can add milk if the coffee tastes too bitter. Inside a sealed can, the flavor must be settled before you open it.

lines.source: 加熱後的味道，要靠什麼繼續調整？
lines.text: What could they use to keep adjusting the flavor after heating?

lines.source: 報導寫，他們持續喝試作品，尋找咖啡、奶和糖的成分比率，設法減少加熱後留下的味道。
lines.text: The report says they kept tasting prototypes, seeking the proportions of coffee, milk and sugar that would reduce the flavor left by heating.

lines.source: 液體調整好了，外殼就只負責裝著它嗎？
lines.text: Once the liquid was adjusted, was the outer shell merely there to hold it?

lines.source: 金屬罐也會參與。UCC後來說，罐裡的鐵離子，會和咖啡中的成分結合。
lines.text: The metal can played a part too. UCC later said iron ions inside the can would combine with components in the coffee.

lines.source: 原廠把那個成分寫作單寧；發生反應以後，奶咖會變得很黑。
lines.text: The maker named that component as tannin. After the reaction, the milk coffee would turn very dark.

lines.source: 你以為外殼只是方便拿，現在卻連飲料的樣子，都可能被它改掉。
lines.text: You think the shell only makes it easy to carry. Now it could even alter what the drink looks like.

lines.source: 要改的地方，這次在罐內側；誰能把咖啡和那層金屬隔開？
lines.text: This time, the change had to be inside the can. Who could separate the coffee from that layer of metal?

lines.source: UCC說，他們和製罐公司合作，開發在罐內施加特殊塗層的技術。
lines.text: UCC says it worked with a can manufacturer to develop technology for applying a special coating inside the can.

lines.source: 那層處理對付的是罐壁帶來的變色，讓咖啡不用直接和裸露的金屬打交道。
lines.text: That treatment addressed discoloration caused by the can wall, keeping coffee from direct contact with bare metal.

lines.source: 我覺得有意思的是，設計一杯能帶走的奶咖，最後還得把包材的做法一起改。
lines.text: What interests me is that designing milk coffee to go eventually meant changing how the packaging was made too.

lines.source: 原廠記下，四月開始販售；可是，有人願意買一罐，帶離原本喝咖啡的地方嗎？
lines.text: The maker records that sales began in April. But would anyone buy a can and take it away from where they usually drank coffee?

lines.source: 上島達司在金氏世界紀錄的訪談裡回憶，剛開始，業界有人把罐裝咖啡當成邪道。
lines.text: In a Guinness World Records interview, Tatsushi Ueshima recalled that some in the industry initially regarded canned coffee as heresy.

lines.source: 受訪者說，也有店家在喝過之後，願意把這種奶咖留下來賣；先試到那一口，才有貨架上的位置。
lines.text: The interviewee said some shopkeepers agreed to stock it after tasting it. That first sip came before its place on the shelf.

lines.source: 最初放進食品店的那幾箱，後來有人接著訂嗎？
lines.text: Did anyone reorder after those first few cases entered food shops?

lines.source: 受訪者說，訂貨慢慢從十箱，到三十箱；這些罐子，是一點一點進到店裡的。
lines.text: The interviewee said orders gradually grew from ten cases to thirty. The cans found their way into shops little by little.

lines.source: 你在食品店原本找的是熟悉的東西，讓新罐子先出現在那裡，才有機會被拿起來。
lines.text: You originally went into a food shop for familiar things. Putting the new can there gave it a chance to be picked up.

lines.source: 但少數店裡賣得動，怎麼讓更多趕路的人，知道這種喝法？
lines.text: But selling in a few shops was one thing. How could more people on the move discover this way of drinking coffee?

lines.source: 原廠回顧，銷售人員會在車站賣店大聲指名購買，再把買到的罐子帶上列車。
lines.text: The maker later recalled salespeople loudly asking for the product by name at station shops, then taking the cans they bought onto trains.

lines.source: 採訪還記下，他們把幾罐排在車窗旁，讓其他乘客看得見。
lines.text: The interview also records them lining up several cans by train windows so other passengers could see them.

lines.source: 你在車廂裡能看到的商品，多了一個不同於咖啡杯的形狀；罐子也變成展示的地方。
lines.text: Among the products you could see in the carriage was a shape unlike a coffee cup. The can became display space too.

lines.source: 我覺得這個動作很小，卻很貼題：要讓人相信能帶著走，就得真的把它帶出去。
lines.text: I find this a small but fitting action: to convince people it could travel, they had to take it traveling.

lines.source: 可是，這樣的推銷仍沒有立刻讓大家熟悉它；哪裡能讓各地來的人，同時遇上這罐奶咖？
lines.text: Yet that promotion didn't make it familiar overnight. Where could people from many places encounter the same can of milk coffee?

lines.source: 採訪報導寫，UCC在籌備萬博生意時，對這個活動會有多大，起初還沒有概念。
lines.text: An interview report says that when UCC began preparing for Expo business, it initially had little sense of the event's scale.

lines.source: 公司內部一度只想像，來客大約十萬人；主管真正出去看，這個判斷還站得住嗎？
lines.text: At one point, people in the company imagined about 100,000 visitors. Would that estimate hold when managers went to look for themselves?

lines.source: 主管到海外視察，發現規模遠超過原先想法，於是把萬博列進銷售策略。
lines.text: Managers inspected overseas and found a scale far beyond their initial expectations, so they brought the Expo into their sales strategy.

lines.source: 隔年三月，大阪的日本萬國博覽會開幕，原本要逐家店介紹的商品，有了另一個接觸場域。
lines.text: The following March, the Japan World Exposition opened in Osaka. A product previously introduced shop by shop gained another place to meet customers.

lines.source: 後來接受採訪的UCC館長說，他們沿著咖啡生產國的聯繫，去接觸參展的國家。
lines.text: UCC's museum director later said in an interview that they used their links with coffee-producing countries to contact participating nations.

lines.source: 展館裡的咖啡店和餐飲空間，需要供貨；UCC本來就在做的咖啡生意，這時派上了用場。
lines.text: Coffee shops and dining spaces in the pavilions needed supplies. UCC's existing coffee business now came into play.

lines.source: 可是，簽到供貨機會，並不會自己把一罐冷飲送到攤位。罐子要從哪裡接上會場？
lines.text: But securing a supply opportunity doesn't deliver a cold can to a stall by itself. Where would cans connect to the Expo site?

lines.source: 他們在大阪製造工廠旁，設了大阪北支店，當時又被稱作萬博支店。
lines.text: They set up the Osaka North Branch beside the Osaka manufacturing plant. At the time, it was also called the Expo Branch.

lines.source: 奶咖先在這個配送據點冷卻，再由卡車送進會場；採訪記述，為此準備了多台車。
lines.text: Milk coffee was chilled at this distribution base before trucks took it to the site. The interview says several vehicles were prepared for this.

lines.source: 我更好奇，會場以外的人，要怎麼知道這罐奶咖？
lines.text: I'm more curious about how people outside the Expo would hear about this milk coffee.

lines.source: 會場裡，來客開始拿起這種罐裝飲料；原廠留下的當時照片，也能看到人手裡的奶咖罐。
lines.text: Visitors at the site began picking up the canned drink. Period photos preserved by the maker also show cans of milk coffee in people's hands.

lines.source: 來自各地的人，把喝過的經驗帶回家鄉；那罐飲料的消息，跟著旅程走出了會場。
lines.text: People from different places took their experience home. News of the drink traveled beyond the Expo with them.

lines.source: 採訪還說，來客拿罐的樣子，被電視帶進家庭，讓沒到現場的人也看見了。
lines.text: The interview also says television brought images of visitors holding cans into homes, reaching people who hadn't been there.

lines.source: 後來，詢問和訂單湧來；連原先不願理會這罐奶咖的通路，也開始來要貨。
lines.text: Later, inquiries and orders poured in. Even sales channels that had previously ignored this milk coffee began asking for stock.

lines.source: 要貨的人多了，貨就一定出得來嗎？
lines.text: If more people want stock, does that mean enough stock can be made?

lines.source: 原廠回顧，到了夏天，需求更旺；工廠全力生產，仍然追不上。
lines.text: The maker recalls that demand grew stronger in summer. Even producing at full capacity, the factory couldn't keep up.

lines.source: UCC主管在採訪裡說，為了貨一做出來就運走，工廠外出現了等待出貨的卡車。
lines.text: A UCC manager said in an interview that trucks waited outside the factory so products could leave as soon as they were made.

lines.source: 你買的是一罐，配送端卻得一批批接貨；多出來的需要，最後落在工廠門外。
lines.text: You buy one can, but distribution must collect batch after batch. The extra demand ultimately arrived at the factory gate.

lines.source: 我覺得這時才看得出交付的重量：想喝的人已經出現，做的人還得追上。
lines.text: I think this is where you feel the weight of delivery: people ready to drink had appeared, and the makers still had to catch up.

lines.source: 一座工廠供應不來時，接貨的缺口怎麼補？
lines.text: When one factory couldn't supply enough, how could they fill the gap?

lines.source: 採訪記下，公司把協力工廠擴展到各地，讓供應不再只靠原先那一座。
lines.text: The interview records the company expanding its network of partner factories across regions, so supply no longer depended on the original plant alone.

lines.source: 上島達司的回憶，也把鐵道弘濟會的採用列為轉點，奶咖於是有了接觸更多旅客的通路。
lines.text: Tatsushi Ueshima's recollection also lists adoption by the Railway Welfare Association as a turning point, giving the milk coffee a route to more travelers.

lines.source: 而你站到販售處，真正拿起初代罐時，還有一個小動作得完成。
lines.text: And when you reached a sales counter and actually picked up that original can, one small action still remained.

lines.source: 原廠初代罐的說明，寫的是用專用開孔器在罐頂開孔；這些孔，各有什麼用？
lines.text: The maker's description of the original can says to pierce its top with a dedicated opener. What did those holes each do?

lines.source: 一邊是飲口，另一邊是空氣孔；喝的人要用它，還得有能把這些入口打開的工具。
lines.text: One was for drinking, the other for air. To use them, you still needed a tool that could open those passages.

lines.source: 你現在熟悉的拉開就喝，在那種罐頂上，還不是手指自己能完成的事。
lines.text: The pull-open-and-drink action you're familiar with today wasn't something fingers alone could accomplish on that can top.

lines.source: 這款奶咖把喝咖啡的地點帶走，卻沒有省掉讓你喝到的工作；那些工作，被接到製造、配送和罐頂。
lines.text: This milk coffee carried coffee drinking beyond its usual place, but it didn't remove the work of getting the drink to you. That work went into manufacturing, distribution and the can top.

lines.source: 你第一次喝罐裝飲料，記得是別人替你開好，還是你自己打開？留言告訴我。
lines.text: Do you remember your first canned drink? Did someone open it for you, or did you open it yourself? Tell me in the comments.

lines.source: 想看懂熟悉物品怎麼把方便交到你手上，歡迎訂閱，一起看那些小動作背後的選擇。
lines.text: To see how familiar objects put convenience in your hands, subscribe and explore the choices behind those small actions with me.
